mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility over the past four weeks (rising from -28.6% to -19.6%) signals normalization of commuting patterns. This trend will continue to drive weekday retail footfall recovery, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to decline below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT station suppression (stable at -45% to -51%) indicates sustained avoidance of public transport. This behavioral shift will constrain RETAIL_REC recovery because transit-dependent populations cannot easily access retail destinations, keeping retail mobility depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains at -45.6% in most recent week with no recovery trend
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility recovers above -35% within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite TRANSIT remaining below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply from -9.4% to -18.0% over four weeks, signaling reduced outdoor leisure activity. This decline in recreational substitutes will redirect discretionary mobility back toward retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 8.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility stabilizes or recovers above -12% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to baseline within the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between WORKPLACES recovery and RESIDENTIAL normalization (RESIDENTIAL declining from +9.6% to +6.9%) indicates a shift in time allocation away from home toward work and retail. This dual reallocation will amplify RETAIL_REC gains beyond what WORKPLACES recovery alone would produce over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20% AND RESIDENTIAL falls below +8%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL moving in opposite directions
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES reverses below -22% or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above +9%, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility at +7.3% to +7.4% indicates essential-goods access is maintained and consumer confidence in public spaces is not collapsing. This stability will support continued RETAIL_REC recovery as consumers perceive lower infection risk, driving retail mobility higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at +7.3% to +7.4% across all four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines below -12%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved steadily from -15.7% to -10.7% over four weeks, establishing a consistent upward trend. This momentum will persist as seasonal factors and behavioral adaptation continue, producing further RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 5 percentage points over four weeks with no reversals
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses to decline below -12% in any of the next two weeks, or the four-week mean does not exceed -10.7%.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between TRANSIT suppression and PARKS decline creates a mobility vacuum where both public transport and outdoor recreation are constrained. Consumers will substitute into retail venues as the only accessible discretionary destination, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both TRANSIT and PARKS are at multi-week lows
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or PARKS recovers above their respective thresholds within one week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery combined with GROCERY_PHARM stability signals that essential mobility patterns are normalizing and public-space confidence is intact. This dual signal will trigger a threshold effect where consumers re-engage with retail, but only if WORKPLACES crosses above -20% and GROCERY_PHARM sustains above +7%, producing RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series have reached recovery thresholds
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls back below -22% or GROCERY_PHARM drops below +6.5% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the prior four-week mean by week 4.
